newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council to discusses Arab request for meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council to discusses Arab request for meeting.

text.p: The Security Council will hold informal consultations on Friday on a request by the Arab group for a meeting on Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in East Jerusalem, council president Njuguna Mahugu of Kenya said on Thursday.
The formal request, received by the council on Thursday, was for an immediate meeting -- which in U.N. terms denotes urgency. But council members said no debate was expected until early next week.

The council is scheduled to consult privately on Friday on several issues and diplomats speculated a Middle East debate might not take place until Tuesday or Wednesday, after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat completes a previously scheduled visit to Washington.

He arrives in Washington late Sunday for meetings the following day with President Bill Clinton and other U.S. officials and might not wish his visit to be distracted by an acrimonious U.N. debate, the diplomats said. He travels to New York Tuesday.

Asked whether Arafat might take part in a Security Council debate, the Palestine Liberation Organisation's U.N. observer, Nasser al-Kidwa, who is chairman of the Arab group, said: "We are working on this (council) issue separately from the visit of President Arafat. But there is of course the possibility if he is around he might give some attention to this issue, of course, since it is an important issue."

The Arab group's request for council action was prompted by an Israeli ministerial committee's approval on Wednesday of plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem captured by Israel during the 1967 war. The site is called Jabal Abu Ghneim by Palestinians and Har Homa by Israel.
Al-Kidwa said that while in New York Arafat would see Secretary-General Kofi Annan and have other meetings, including with the Council on Foreign Relations and some Jewish leaders.

On Wednesday afternoon he flies to Houston to see former President George Bush and former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker and to deliver a lecture at the James Baker Institute for public policy at Rice University, al-Kidwa said.
Arafat is to return home Wednesday night.
